front: What was autocracy in Tsarist Russia?
back: Rule by the Tsar, whose power was not limited by any parliament or law and who claimed authority from God.
A policy of making non-Russian peoples use the Russian language and institutions (and often the Orthodox faith).

front: When was Alexander II assassinated, and by whom?
back: 13 March 1881 (1 March in the old calendar), by members of the People's Will.
Procurator of the Holy Synod from 1880 and adviser to Alexander III, who opposed parliaments and religious toleration.

front: What did Bunge do as Minister of Finance (1881-87)?
back: Reduced redemption payments, founded the Peasants' Land Bank (1882) and brought in factory inspectors and child-labour limits.
Nobles appointed to supervise the peasant villages with judicial and administrative powers.

front: Who founded the first Russian Marxist group and when?
back: George Plekhanov founded Emancipation of Labour in 1883, in exile in Switzerland.

front: Why did Alexander III turn from reform to repression?
back: His father's murder convinced him that reform had encouraged revolutionaries, and Pobedonostsev urged him to defend the autocracy.

front: Why did rapid industrialisation create problems for the Tsarist regime?
back: It burdened the peasants and created a working class without rights, who became an audience for Marxist ideas.
